canonical_question: Why was the CIP pressure limited to 400 MPa, and would higher pressures improve green density significantly?

question_variants.question: Why was the CIP pressure limited to 400 MPa, and would higher pressures improve green density significantly?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document states CIP pressure was limited to 400 MPa but does not provide the reason for this limitation, nor does it offer data on whether higher pressures would improve green density.

answers.answer: The text specifies that compaction was performed under 400 MPa pressure, but offers no rationale for this limit or data comparing it to higher pressures.
answers.measurement_outcome: No density data or comparison provided
answers.boundary_limitation: No explanation for pressure limit or higher pressure outcomes.
evidence_spans: Several methods of powder metallurgy were used to prepare the equimolar HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Elemental powders (purity >99%) and granularity of −325 mesh (<44 μm) were supplied by Huarui Co. (Chengdu, China).
Weighting and mixing of powders was performed under Ar protective atmosphere.

source_evidence_spans: pressed into green compacts (denoted here HEAP) using CIP under the pressure of 400 MPa
